article.title: How to Install a Closet Shelf and Rod
article.summary: Install a sturdy closet shelf and hanging rod: set the right heights, screw cleats into studs, add a center bracket for long spans, and level everything.
article.body:
A wood shelf and rod on cleats screwed into studs holds far more than wire shelving clipped into drywall. This guide covers a standard reach-in closet with a single shelf and one hanging rod.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: wear safety glasses when cutting and drilling. Check for wires and pipes before you drill: outlets, switches and plumbing on the other side of the wall are clues.

Steps

  1. Mark the heights

    For a single rod, a common layout puts the rod about 66 in off the floor and the shelf just above it, around 68 to 70 in. Draw a level line at the shelf height on the back wall and both side walls. Mark the stud locations on the back wall with a stud finder.

    Done right: a level line runs around the three walls and studs are marked on the back wall.

  2. Install the cleats

    Cut 1x4 cleats to fit the back wall and both side walls. Hold their top edge on your line and screw them into each stud with two 2-1/2 in screws. On side walls without studs at the right spot, use heavy-duty drywall anchors rated for the load.

    Done right: the cleats don't move when you pull down on them hard.

  3. Mount the rod sockets

    Screw a closet rod socket to each side cleat, centered about 12 in out from the back wall. That distance lets hangers swing freely.

    Done right: both sockets are at the same height and the same distance from the back wall.

  4. Add a center support for long spans

    If the rod spans more than about 4 ft, add a shelf-and-rod bracket into a stud near the middle. Without it, the rod and shelf will sag under the weight of clothes.

    Done right: no part of the rod spans more than about 4 ft without support.

  5. Set the shelf and rod

    Cut the shelf to the closet width, 1/8 in short so it drops in easily. Rest it on the cleats and bracket, and drive 1-1/4 in screws down through it into the cleats. Cut the rod to length and drop it into the sockets and bracket.

    Done right: the shelf is level and the rod doesn't rattle in its sockets.

Hire a carpenter or closet company if: you want a full custom system with drawers and towers, or the walls are plaster over lath where finding studs and drilling is harder.

FAQ

How high should a closet rod be?

About 66 in for a single rod. For a double-hang closet, about 80 to 84 in for the top rod and 40 to 42 in for the bottom rod.

How far should a closet rod be from the back wall?

About 12 in from the back wall to the center of the rod, so hangers don't hit the wall.

How long can a closet rod span without support?

Plan for a support bracket about every 4 ft. Longer spans sag with a full load of clothes.

Wood or wire closet shelving?

Wood or plywood shelves on stud-mounted cleats are stronger and don't leave marks on folded clothes. Wire is cheaper and lets air circulate.
